Mississauga sellers: that renovation may backfire.

A big project does not always pay back what it costs. 1) Ask your Realtor® which fixes buyers in your area notice most. 2) Compare any renovation quote with what updated homes nearby sold for. 3) Repair leaks, broken fixtures and safety items before listing. 4) Skip big taste-based projects; fresh, neutral paint is often the safer choice.

Milton: what does a 1% higher rate do to the monthly mortgage on a $700K home? Here is the math.

Example only, Canadian semi-annual compounding, 25-year amortization:
1) $700,000 minus 20% down ($140,000) leaves a $560,000 mortgage.
2) At 4.95%, the monthly mortgage is about $3,241 (principal and interest only).
3) At 5.95%, it is about $3,566.
4) The difference is about $325 every month.
Source for the example rate: the uninsured 5-year fixed rate shown on nesto.ca on Nov 16, 2026; 5.95% is that rate plus one percentage point. Your rate depends on your down payment, lender and term. Property tax, heat and insurance are extra.

Etobicoke condo: unseen fees could hit.

Before you sign, look past the unit itself. 1) Ask your lawyer to review the condo's status certificate before your conditions end. 2) Check what it says about the reserve fund and any special assessments. 3) Ask what the monthly condo fees cover and how they have changed. 4) Ask whether the condo corporation is involved in any legal proceedings.

caption:
Georgetown: passed inspection. Still risky?

A clean inspection report is useful, but it is a snapshot, not a guarantee. 1) Remember it covers what the inspector could see that day. 2) Ask which areas could not be checked or reached. 3) Ask how old the roof, furnace and windows are. 4) Set aside a repair fund for your first year in the home.
